item.text:
It makes sense to feel unsure. Alex’s daily attention and strong declarations after six weeks could reflect genuine enthusiasm, but “you’re the only person who understands me” can also create pressure to feel responsible for their wellbeing. That doesn’t establish deliberate manipulation or fraud. Work and travel constraints may explain the delayed meeting; they aren’t evidence that Alex has refused a video call.

Slow the pace and set a clear boundary: “I want to keep getting to know you, but I need time offline and don’t want to be your only source of support.” Notice whether Alex respects that without making you feel guilty. Suggest a live video conversation as one way to learn more—not proof of identity or safety. Talk through the messages with someone you trust while keeping your usual relationships and routines.

No financial request is described. If one arises later, don’t send money or gifts to an online-only contact. If Alex starts pressuring you to withdraw from others or repeatedly ignores your boundaries, step back from contact.
